manifest.name: dsh-web-search-doubao
manifest.description: Doubao Search (Volcengine) web search provider for DeepSeek Harness — registers into the ctx.web seam so the standard web_search tool returns real excerpts.

bundle.text:
# ============================================================================
# dsh-web-search-doubao — DeepSeek Harness bundle patch
#
# Inserts one row: this package's own. Mounting it runs `apply()`, which
#
#   1. registers the Doubao-backed WebSearchProvider with the `ctx.web` seam;
#   2. selects that provider for as long as the row stays mounted, handing the
#      seam's previous selection back when it is disposed.
#
# The selection deliberately is NOT a `- id: web` patch here. A row patch is
# applied for as long as the bundle is selected, so a hardcoded
# `searchProvider: doubao` would outlive the plugin being disabled and leave the
# seam naming a provider that no longer exists — the seam then answers
# WEB_PROVIDER_CONFIGURED_MISSING instead of falling back to the shipped
# provider. Taking the selection in `apply()` keeps enable/disable symmetric:
# with the plugin off the seam resolves exactly as it did before install.
#
# Note that a row patch REPLACES the targeted row's whole `config`, which is
# another reason not to patch `web` here: it would silently unset the seam's
# `fetchProvider` and break web_fetch.
#
# If you prefer a fixed selection instead, set it in your profile's own patch
# layer (applied after every bundle layer) — but then it is your job to keep it
# pointed at a provider that is actually registered:
#
#   - id: web
#     config:
#       searchProvider: doubao
#       fetchProvider: http
# ============================================================================

- insert:
    - id: web-search-doubao
      name: 'dsh-web-search-doubao'

readme.text:
Give DeepSeek Harness's standard **`web_search`** tool a search backend that returns
**real excerpts**, not just titles and links.

This is a **search provider plugin** for the harness's web capability seam (`ctx.web`).
It registers a Doubao Search (Volcengine) backend and points the seam at it, so the
model-facing tool `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-web` keeps working unchanged — only the
backend behind it changes.

English | [中文](./README.zh.md)

---

The harness ships `@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-search-deepseek`, which performs search by
asking a model to call the **server-side `web_search` tool** over an
Anthropic-compatible Messages API. That route works, but the results it can surface
carry only a **title and a URL** — the response has no citation excerpts, so the
normalized `sources[].snippet` is always empty.

The Doubao Search API is a plain search endpoint that returns structured results,
including a per-result body. This plugin maps that body onto `snippet`, so every
source arrives with text the model can actually read and cite:

| | model-side `web_search` tool | this plugin (Doubao Search API) |
|---|---|---|
| `sources[].title` / `.url` | ✅ | ✅ |
| `sources[].snippet` | ❌ always empty | ✅ real excerpt per source |
| `sources[].publishedAt` | sometimes the `1970-01-01` epoch sentinel | real date, sentinel filtered out |
| Cost per search | one extra model turn (thousands of tokens) | one API call, no model tokens |
| Typical latency | 6–14 s | ~0.2–0.6 s |

- DeepSeek Harness `>= 0.2.0-rc.2` (the `ctx.web` seam's provider API).
- Node.js `>= 22`.
- A **Volcengine API key**. An **Agent Plan** key works here and draws on the plan's
  AFP quota — the official Agent Plan docs describe Doubao Search as the plan's search
  service, callable with the plan's dedicated API key. A key from an unrelated
  Volcengine product will authenticate but is not covered by the plan.

The endpoint defaults to `https://open.feedcoopapi.com/search_api/web_search`, which is
the public Doubao Search URL. No configuration is needed to reach it.
```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:gilsaia/dsh-web-search-doubao

dsh plugin --profile web add /path/to/dsh-web-search-doubao
```

The package declares `dsh.bundle.patch`, so adding it also adds it to the profile's
bundle list, and its patch selects this provider:
yaml
- insert:
    - id: web-search-doubao
      name: 'dsh-web-search-doubao'

- id: web
  config:
    searchProvider: doubao
    fetchProvider: http
```

`fetchProvider` is restated because a row patch **replaces** the targeted row's whole
`config`; omitting it would unset the fetch provider and break `web_fetch`.

> **About the `Issues with peer dependencies found` warning:** it is expected. The
> `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` packages this plugin imports are provided by the harness itself
> at load time rather than installed into the profile, so pnpm reports them as missing
> peers. The harness resolves them when it mounts the plugin.
Restart the harness afterwards (or reload the profile), then run a search.

The plugin ships a **client half**. After one restart it adds a **联网搜索 (Web search)**
page to the harness settings sidebar, and everything below can be done there:

- **API Key** — typed into a password field and written through the harness credentials
  domain under the reference the form names. The literal never enters a settings file,
  and the page only learns whether a key is *configured*, not what it is.
- **Every config field** — endpoint, search type, result count, time range, authority
  filter, query rewriting, summary toggle. Fields you changed show **未保存**; fields the
  user layer overrides show **已覆盖** with a one-click **恢复默认**.
- **Save** applies one revision-fenced write; **撤销** discards the staged edits.

A save takes effect on the next search — no restart needed for either the config or the
key. The page mounts only while the host serves the `web-search-doubao` settings
namespace, so a deployment without the plugin shows no trace of it.

readme.section: Provide the key without the GUI
readme.text:
The plugin requires a key. It resolves one in this order:

1. the literal **`apiKey`** config value;
2. the credential named by **`apiKeyEnv`** (default `ARK_API_KEY`), read through the
   harness credentials service, falling back to the launching environment.

So either export it:

```sh
export ARK_API_KEY=...        # then start the harness
```

or set it in the plugin's config in the profile's patch layer:

readme.section: Provide the key without the GUI
readme.text:
```yaml
- id: web-search-doubao
  config:
    apiKey: '...'             # a secret; prefer apiKeyEnv so no key enters a config file
```

> If the profile patch is still the shipped default, it contains a bare `[]`. Replace that
> `[]` with your entries — appending a `- id:` item after it makes the file two YAML
> documents and the harness refuses to parse the overlay.

readme.section: Provide the key without the GUI
readme.text:
A missing key fails the search with `WEB_PROVIDER_CREDENTIAL_MISSING` and a message
naming the reference that was consulted — it never silently returns zero results.

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `apiKey` | string (secret) | — | Literal API key. |
| `apiKeyEnv` | credential ref | `ARK_API_KEY` | Credential reference resolved per search. |
| `baseURL` | string | Doubao Search URL | Full endpoint; override for a proxy or a different region. |
| `searchType` | `web` \| `image` | `web` | `image` returns image results instead of pages. |
| `maxResults` | 1–50 | `10` | Result count when a request carries no bound. |
| `timeRange` | string | — | `OneDay` / `OneWeek` / `OneMonth` / `OneYear`, or `YYYY-MM-DD..YYYY-MM-DD`. |
| `authLevel` | 0–2 | `0` | `1` restricts to authoritative sources. Web searches only. |
| `queryRewrite` | boolean | `false` | Let the service rewrite a conversational query into a search-shaped one. |
| `needSummary` | boolean | `true` | Request the excerpt surfaced as `snippet`. Turning this off empties `snippet`. |

`baseURL` can also be overridden with the `DOUBAO_SEARCH_BASE_URL` environment variable.

Every field is read **per search**, so a settings change applies to the next search
without restarting the harness.

The plugin takes the seam's provider selection **while it is mounted** and hands the
previous selection back when it unmounts, so the ordinary plugin switch is the switch:

- **Enabled** — the provider registers and the seam selects `doubao`; searches use Doubao
  Search.
- **Disabled** — the provider unregisters and the previous selection is restored. With no
  explicit selection the seam auto-selects the only remaining usable provider, which is
  the shipped DeepSeek one.

Nothing is written into your profile patch, so disabling genuinely returns the harness to
its pre-install state. That is why the bundle patch deliberately carries **no** `- id: web`
row patch: a row patch outlives the plugin being disabled and would leave the seam naming
a provider that no longer exists — the seam answers `WEB_PROVIDER_CONFIGURED_MISSING` and
does not fall back.

If you want the **shipped** provider to be usable while this plugin is off, configure it
directly; that is independent of this plugin. Its default endpoint is
`https://api.deepseek.com/anthropic/v1`, which will not accept a key minted for a different
platform:

```yaml
- id: web-search-deepseek
  config:
    baseURL: https://ark.cn-beijing.volces.com/api/plan/v1   # an Anthropic-compatible endpoint
```

To pin the selection explicitly instead, do it in your own patch layer (applied after every
bundle layer) — but then keeping it pointed at a registered provider is your responsibility,
and disabling this plugin while it is pinned to `doubao` will error:

```yaml
- id: web
  config:
    searchProvider: doubao
    fetchProvider: http
```sh

readme.section: pure-function and plugin-contract tests: no network, no key
readme.text: npm test

readme.section: live check against the real API; asserts sources carry snippets
readme.text:
ARK_API_KEY=... npm run test:live
```

To confirm the composition without booting:

```sh
dsh --profile web --dump-config | grep -A4 'id: web$'

- `provider.js` — `DoubaoSearchProvider`, the wire format, result mapping, and error
  translation. It uses the native `fetch` client and does **not** go through `ctx.llm`.
- `index.js` — the Cordis plugin: `name`, `inject: ['web']`, the `Config` schema, and
  `apply()`, which registers the provider into the seam.
- `client/client.js` — the browser half, declared as `dsh.client` and served by the host
  under `/plugins`. Hand-authored against the loader's client-bundle envelope, so it
  needs no build step and requires only the platform `react`. Every read and write goes
  through the documented Remote namespaces (`settings.describe` / `settings.mutate` /
  `credentials.describe` / `credentials.set`).
- `cordis.patch.yml` — the bundle patch that mounts the plugin. It does not touch the
  seam's selection: `apply()` takes it on mount and returns it on disposal, so
  enable/disable stays symmetric (see *Turning it on and off*).

Two details worth knowing if you fork it:

- The API answers failures with **HTTP 200** and an `Error` object under
  `ResponseMetadata`, so a successful status code is not enough — the body is checked
  too.
- The API emits an epoch sentinel (`1970-01-01T08:00:00+08:00`) for pages whose crawl
  time is unknown. That is filtered out rather than surfaced as a publication date.

`@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` peer dependencies are declared as open ranges (`>=0.2.0-rc.2`)
rather than pinned, so the plugin keeps working across harness release candidates.
DeepSeek Harness is in developer preview and may change the seam's API; if a future
version does, this plugin needs the same update as any other provider.
